The *Bījaṅgapañha* ("The Seed", Mil 7.3.3) is a short discourse in the *Opammakathāpañha* (Book 7) of the *Milindapañha* [SuttaCentral]. Following the characteristic pattern of the seventh book, the text draws an analogy between the spiritual practice of a practitioner and the specific qualities or attributes (*aṅga*) of a seed (*bīja*) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records three modern translations in three languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

No formal parallels are cataloged for this section on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. However, DharmaNexus identifies substantial internal text reuse across 38 Pali texts (186 matching passages), reflecting the highly formulaic framework shared with other simile-based questions in the seventh book of the *Milindapañha*, most notably the *Meghaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.7.6), *Bhojanaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.8.6), *Pavanaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.7.4), *Cakkavākaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.6.2), and *Nāvālagganakaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.3.6) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus records a match between segments 1.2–1.3 of the Pali text and the Tibetan translation of the *Mahāsūtrasamuccaya* (*Mdo kun las btus pa chen po*, D3961) [DharmaNexus].
